base_member_text: byte-identical duplicate of multi_vessel_morphology/mk_depth.F; same observations apply: depth can go negative for large abs(Y) without clipping, X/Y arrays are never written, bathy_param.txt content order only implicit in READ sequence (L9-L15)
audit_member_text: No bounds/physical validation prevents nonpositive Mglob/Nglob/DX/DY, negative width, or slopes large enough to make DEPTH negative outside the channel (L9-L35).

The y-coordinate formula L24 is not cell-centered symmetrically for even Nglob: it yields indices from `(1-Nglob/2)*DY` through `(Nglob/2)*DY` (for Nglob=100, -49*DY through +50*DY). Because bank depth uses abs(Y) at L30-L32, the two sides contain unequal coordinate extents and can receive asymmetric depth values despite symmetric input parameters.

The output format has exactly 9000 F descriptors at L41 while the implied-DO writes Mglob values at L39. If Mglob exceeds 9000, Fortran format reversion can continue the same J values on another record, breaking the intended one-grid-row-per-record layout.
OPEN/READ/ALLOCATE/WRITE have no IOSTAT or size checks, so missing/malformed input and allocation/output failures are uncontrolled.
